newsitem.title: USA: Idaho approves Wash. Water Power tariff.
newsitem.headline: Idaho approves Wash. Water Power tariff.

text.p: The Idaho Public Utilities Commission on Friday approved Washington Water Power Co's proposal to allow certain large industrial customers to choose their own power supplier.

Under the direct access tariff, submitted by the utility for review in May, 30 of Washington Water Power's customers have the option to choose an alternative supplier for up to one-third of their electricity load. Transmission service from the utility will be provided at a rate of 1.284 cents per kilowatt hour (KWh).
The trial program is effective immediately and will expire August 31, 1998.
WWP said the experimental program will not affect rates for other customer classes.

On July 1, the Washington Utilities and Transportation Commission approved a similar tariff, with a rate of 1.547 cents per KWh, and three customers have opted to take service under that pilot program, the company said.
WWP provides electricity service to customers in eastern Washington and northern Idaho, and provides natural gas service to customers in parts of Washington, Idaho, Oregon and California.
